The user wants me to act as Evidence Critic and check each claim against the cited evidence. I need to flag only factual problems: overstatements, wrong numbers/dates/suppliers, causes not stated, products/NDCs not in evidence. Reasonable conclusions from cited facts are supported.

Let me examine each claim:

Claim 1: investigator: "Our package NDC 63323-852-25 is on the FDA shortage list as 'Available' with note to check wholesalers for inventory." Cited: [shortage-63323-852-25]

Evidence says: "FDA shortage list: Hydromorphone Hydrochloride, Injection, 1 mg/1 mL (NDC 63323-852-25) from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC; availability: 'Available'; Check wholesalers for inventory; updated 10/15/2026"

This matches exactly. The claim says "Available" with note to check wholesalers for inventory. Evidence says availability: "Available"; Check wholesalers for inventory. Supported.

Claim 2: investigator: "Current stock of 39 units covers only 5.2 days at 7.5 units per day." Cited: [stock-16]

Evidence says: "hydromorphone HYDROMORPHONE HYDROCHLORIDE 1 mg/mL (Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC, NDC 63323-852-25, NDA019034, critical drug): 39 units on hand, 7.5/day over 30 days, 5.2 days of cover"

Matches exactly. Supported.

Claim 3: investigator: "No ongoing recall for this NDC." Cited: [search-recall-16]

Evidence says: "Searched this run's FDA ongoing-recall snapshot for our package NDC 63323-852-25 and product 63323-852: no ongoing recall."

Matches. Supported.

All claims appear supported. No factual problems. So unsupported list empty.
